user_query: Why does LINE's use of DeepWalk on the Youtube network make the comparison especially fair for large-scale graphs?
llm_response: LINE’s use of DeepWalk on the YouTube network is especially fair for large-scale graphs because YouTube is a very large graph, and DeepWalk is one of the few baseline methods that can still be run at that scale. That means the comparison is not biased by choosing a baseline that only works well on small graphs or that cannot feasibly be applied to the same large dataset. In other words, LINE is being compared against a scalable random-walk embedding method on a graph where scalability really matters, so the evaluation better reflects performance on large-scale settings rather than on toy or small graphs.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a well-supported interpretation of why a scalable baseline on a large graph makes the comparison fair, though the exact wording depends on the original paper’s framing.
